transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Uh, hi. I guess... well, people just keep getting on my case, saying I'm not listening to them. My supervisor at work, or my wife. They'll be talking straight to me, and... I don't know. A minute later I realize I only caught half of it. Then I have to ask them to say it all again. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
Did these attention problems start when you were a child?

Yeah... I guess I was like this even as a kid. Teachers were always, um, moving my seat around. Said I couldn't stay put. I'd just... call out answers. Got in trouble a bit for butting into other kids' work... this was before middle school, mostly. So... yeah.
Do you still feel physically restless or like you have to move around a lot?

Yeah... I guess so. Sitting around just... it gets to me. 

If I have to just sit still, I get this... pressure building up. Like in my chest, and my legs. Just feels like I gotta move right that second or... I don't know, like I'll crawl out of my skin. So... yeah.
Do you often blurt out answers before a question is finished?

Yeah... I guess. Like, uh... at work, in our meetings. My supervisor will be asking something, and I just... jump in before he's done. 

I'll already be talking, and then I realize I didn't even let him get to the actual important part of the question. It just... comes out. So... yeah. That happens.
